# v0.3.0-dev.1 — the expedition drop

First prerelease of the 0.3 line: token classes, the trust round, offline snapshots, session interchange, per-share link previews, and a large viewer round. Everything below is new since **v0.2.1**.

## Auth: token classes, lineage, enrollment

- **Full vs scoped tokens.** Full tokens are account credentials (create, control all your shares, mint tokens, edit settings). Scoped tokens are service credentials for CI and integrations: they create and manage only their own shares, list only those, and never keep an account alive.
- **Access-code lineage.** One call (`revoke-lineage`) revokes every token ever minted through an access code.
- **Standing freeze.** Revoking a user's last *full* token freezes control of all their shares — both the token path and the share-secret path — while viewing keeps working. Rotation mints the replacement first, so a routine rotate never freezes anything.
- **Codeless onboarding** (server setting, default off): a public server may let users onboard without an access code.
- **Ask-once enrollment.** The TUI asks once per server — enroll with a token or share anonymously — and never silently enrolls.
- Shares record the token that created them, so per-token audit and per-token freeze work after the fact.

## Share settings API

- `PATCH /api/share/:id` — change login/password, TTL and metadata after creation; an auth pair must be both-or-none.
- **Named config sets**: one token can carry multiple named configuration sets; clients fetch and adopt them at boot, so a repo needs only a URL + secret.

## Trust & privacy

- **Hours-native TTLs** everywhere: `ttlHours` in config/env/API, `MAX_TTL_HOURS` cap, 1-hour floor. Legacy day fields convert automatically.
- **Redaction at the sync choke point**: secret shapes (GitHub/AWS/Slack/Google keys, bearer tokens, PEM blocks, `.env` pairs, connection strings) plus custom patterns, replaced with `[redacted:<kind>]` markers before anything leaves the machine.
- **Private facts split**: the session's directory and worktree leave the public item; authenticated readers of gated shares receive them in a private block. The viewer no longer displays session ids.
- **Relative paths on the wire**: tool paths inside the working folder ship relative (`.` for the folder itself, `~/…` under the sharer's home). Applied at serve time, so existing shares benefit too.

## Snapshots — one-file offline shares

- The transcript button downloads a **self-contained HTML snapshot** (~7 MB) that boots from `file://` with full fidelity: file cards, diffs and syntax highlighting run on main-thread copies of the worker modules; only the share's own grammars, icons and fonts are packed. The header reads `snapshot`.
- `tools/osh-snapshot.mjs` — headless/CI downloader with `--login` / `--token` auth.
- `tools/osh-snapshot-local.mjs` — builds the same file straight from `opencode export` output. No share, no network.
- The server-side snapshot endpoint ships off by default (`SNAPSHOT_ENDPOINT=1`): assembling the ~350-chunk graph server-side exceeds the Cloudflare free plan's subrequest cap. The browser button and the CLI are fine everywhere.

## Interchange

- `tools/osh-session.mjs` — export a share (URL, envelope, or export files), pack exports back into a share envelope, and import sessions into opencode through the real `opencode import` (roundtrip-tested). Marked experimental in the docs.
